info.title: HookPulse
info.description: Monitor scheduled tasks and receive alerts for missing check-ins. Read GET /api/ for the API index.

bearerAuth.description: Guest token (`POST /api/guest`) in `X-Guest-Token: hp_…` or `Authorization: Bearer hp_…`. A signed-in account (cookie) also works and takes precedence.

globalAccount.name: __Host-mm-auth
globalAccount.description: Global session in the product's HttpOnly cookie; writes require exact Origin and X-CSRF-Token.

contaChaveApi.description: Account API key: `Authorization: Bearer mmk_…` or `X-Api-Key: mmk_…`. Created on the account page (API keys), valid only in the product where it was created; it acts as the account (or the organization that owns it).

carteiraAgente.description: Wallet credential of an agent without an account (`Authorization: Bearer mmw_…`, 30 days, this product only): POST /api/auth/wallet/agent/start, sign the message with the wallet, POST /api/auth/wallet/agent/token. The owner is `x402:<address>`.

id.description: Monitor ID; it is the `:id` of the ingest URL.

check.description: Only on a site: what HookPulse calls — `url`, `method` (`GET` or `HEAD`), `expect_status` (`200-399`, a range `a-b` or one code), `keyword` (text that must be in the first 64 KB, or `null`) and `timeout_ms`.

site.description: Only on a site: `state` (`waiting`, `up` or `down`), `changed_at` (when it last changed), `last_check_at`, `last_ok`, `last_status` (HTTP status, `null` when nothing answered), `last_reason` (why it failed: `status`, `keyword`, `timeout`, `dns`, `connection`, `tls`, `private_address` or `network`; `null` when it answered), `last_ms` and `certificate_until` (HTTPS certificate expiry).

name.description: Name you gave it, to recognise it in the alert.

interval_sec.description: Tolerated silence, in seconds. Past that, it is a miss. With `cron` set it is read-only and mirrors the schedule's window.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression, when the monitor runs on a schedule instead of an interval.

tz.description: IANA time zone the `cron` is read in.

grace_sec.description: Tolerance after the scheduled time before it counts as late.

next_expected_at.description: When the next scheduled run is due (UTC). Computed forward on creation, on patch and on every ping; late is this plus `grace_sec`.

alert_url.description: HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack, Discord, n8n).

last_event_at.description: Last ping received (UTC); `null` while it never pinged.

last_status.description: HTTP status the last ping sent, when it did.

last_latency_ms.description: Latency reported in the last ping, in ms.

last_start_at.description: When the current run said it started (`/in/:id/start`), while it has not finished.

last_run_id.description: The `rid` of the run that is currently open, when the `start` carried one.

last_duration_ms.description: How long the last run took, measured between its `start` and its outcome.

duration.description: Duration statistics over the last runs we measured: `samples`, `p50_ms` and `max_ms`. `p50_ms` is the low median, so it is always a duration that actually happened. Only on `GET /api/endpoints/:id` — the list does not pay for it. All null when nothing has been measured.

max_duration_sec.description: Ceiling for an open run: past it, the next 5-minute check alerts with `reason: "too_long"`. `null` when it is off.

alert_pending.description: An outcome waiting for the next 5-minute check to alert: `fail`, `recovery`, or `null` when there is nothing pending.

miss_count.description: How many times this monitor has gone silent.

alerts_on_hold.description: `true` when the monitor is beyond what its owner covers. It keeps checking, and its alerts wait for a plan (a guest signs in first). `coverage` on `GET /api/endpoints` tells why. On the list, `GET /api/endpoints/:id` and creation.

alerted_at.description: When the last alert went out — it is what holds the repeat cap.

alert_repeat_sec.description: EFFECTIVE gap before the same incident alerts again: what you asked for, or your `interval_sec` when that is longer, or the 86400 default.

tags.description: The monitor's tags, normalised and sorted. Empty when it has none.

paused_until.description: End of the maintenance window (UTC). While it is in the future the monitor is not checked and never alerts.

state.description: The state in one word: `ok`, `late`, `down` (a site that does not answer), `waiting` (never pinged, or a site not checked yet), `paused` or `inactive`. Read this instead of re-deriving precedence from the booleans.

healthy.description: `true` when it has pinged at least once and is not overdue.

waiting_first_ping.description: `true` while it never pinged. Neither healthy nor overdue: nobody has wired it yet.

ingest_url.description: The URL your cron/webhook calls to prove life. Not on a site: a site does not ping.

token.description: Read token of this monitor. Only comes on creation and to the owner.

status_url.description: Status of this monitor with the token already in the query.

events_url.description: Latest pings with the token already in the query.

curl_example.description: The ingest `curl`, ready to paste in the cron.

templates.description: Ingest snippets and the alert body, with this monitor already in them.

Monitor.description: A monitor. A routine (`kind: "routine"`) is a dead-man switch: the thing you make ping. If the ping stops for longer than `interval_sec` — or, with a schedule, past `next_expected_at` plus `grace_sec` — it becomes `overdue` and the alert goes out. A site (`kind: "site"`) is the other way round: HookPulse calls its `check.url` every `interval_sec` and alerts when it goes down (`state: "down"`) and when it is back.

ingest_curl.description: A `curl` that works as proof of life.

ingest_n8n.description: How to call the ingest from n8n.

miss_json.description: The exact JSON we POST to `alert_url` when a monitor goes bad. `reason` says which way: `silence` (it stopped pinging) or `fail` (it reported an explicit failure).

recovery_json.description: The JSON we POST when the monitor comes back, with `down_since`, `recovered_at` and `downtime_sec`. It has its own `type` (`hookpulse.recovery`) so an integration filtering by type never shows good news as an incident.

miss_url_hint.description: What works as `alert_url` — public HTTPS only.

github_actions.description: A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow with the HookPulse step at the end: no secret, the job's OIDC token identifies the repository.

Templates.description: How to ping, what we send when it fails and what we send when it comes back. It is what saves guessing the format.

post.summary: Creates a monitor: a routine that pings us (silence beyond the interval becomes an alert), or with `check` a site we call.

name.description: Name to recognise the monitor in the alert — it travels in the e-mail subject, the badge and the public dashboard. Required for a routine: we never invent one for you. A site without it is named after its host. Trimmed, at most 80 characters, any alphabet; punctuation alone and invisible characters are rejected.

check.description: Makes the monitor a site: `url` (http or https, public; required), `method` (`GET` or `HEAD`, default `GET`), `expect_status` (what counts as up: `200-399` by default, a range `a-b` or one code), `keyword` (text that must be in the first 64 KB of the page; it forces `GET`) and `timeout_ms` (1000 to 30000, default 10000). Redirects are followed.

interval_sec.description: Tolerated silence, in seconds. Below the free minimum, it costs.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression (`0 3 * * *`). Mutually exclusive with `interval_sec`: with a schedule, the deadline is the scheduled time plus `grace_sec`.

tz.description: IANA time zone the `cron` is read in. Default `UTC`. Only with `cron`.

grace_sec.description: Seconds of tolerance after the scheduled time before it counts as late. Default 90, minimum 30, maximum 86400. Under the free minimum interval it costs, same rule as `interval_sec`.

paused_until.description: Maintenance window: while this UTC instant is in the future the monitor is not checked. At most 30 days ahead.

max_duration_sec.description: Alerts with `reason: "too_long"` when a run opened by `/in/:id/start` has not finished within this many seconds. 60 to 86400; `null` or `0` turns it off. Detection happens on the next 5-minute check.

alert_repeat_sec.description: How long before the SAME incident alerts again. Minimum 3600, maximum 2592000 (30 days, effectively "tell me once"); `null` keeps the default of 86400. Your `interval_sec` is the floor: nothing new happened between two checks.

tags.description: Up to 8 tags to group this monitor: lower-case letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 32 characters each. A comma-separated string works too. We lower-case and de-duplicate, so `Prod` and `prod` are the same tag.

alert_to.description: E-mail to alert on a miss; without it, the account is alerted.

alert_url.description: Public HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack Incoming, Discord, n8n).

400.description: The name answers with a code: `nome_obrigatorio` (missing, empty or blank) or `nome_invalido` (not a string, punctuation only, or carrying control/format characters). Also an invalid interval or an `alert_url` that is not public HTTPS. The schedule answers with a code: `cron_ou_interval` (both sent), `cron_invalido`, `tz_invalida`, `grace_invalido`, `cron_sem_ocorrencia` (never happens within 366 days). The maintenance window answers `pausa_invalida` (not a future instant) or `pausa_longa` (over 30 days). The `check` answers `check_invalid` (not an object), `check_url_invalid`, `check_url_credentials` (user or password in the URL), `check_url_private` (local name or private address), `check_method_invalid`, `check_expect_status_invalid`, `check_keyword_invalid`, `check_timeout_invalid` or `check_with_cron`.

402.description: Payment required. The x402 terms (USDC on Base) come in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header and in `accepts[]`: pay and repeat the same call with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` (x402 v2) or `X-PAYMENT` (v1). A standard x402 client such as `@x402/fetch` does this for you.

post.summary: Paste a `crontab -l` and get one monitor per scheduled line.
post.description:
The body is the crontab itself, as `text/plain`. Without `?apply=1` **nothing is written**: you get the proposal — what would become a monitor, what was ignored and why, and what still fits in the free tier. With `apply=1` it is all or nothing, under the same rules as `POST /api/endpoints`. Comments, variables and `@reboot` are ignored (there is no way to know when to expect a reboot); `@daily` and friends become the equivalent expression. The command becomes the monitor name, with passwords and tokens redacted first — the name travels in the alert e-mail, in the public dashboard and in the badge.
Returns: { applied, recognized, ignored, existing, would_create, created?, free_tier }

The payment releases what was bought by itself: the pack becomes the `cred_…` token already in the response; the balance goes to the logged-in account's organization. The first purchase needs `documento` (CPF or CNPJ, sent to the gateway and not stored here) and `nome`; `email`, `pagina` and `navegador_id` are optional. Set `usd` to an amount from `pacotes` or `exatos` in the GET response. The server sets the amount in cents and rejects amounts that the app has not declared.
